The player's own words named 'Rebecca' before the story has introduced her; the narrator echoed the word and the narration safety guard rejected the turn with HTTP 409 "narration mentions an unavailable entity 'rebecca'". A spine/canon prompt must never name a character, place or thing the player cannot know yet in that scene (see docs/player-input-guide.md and docs/narrator-writing-guide.md). The matcher entry k_sl_1c_c_r2 (data/stories/continuity-initiative/knowledge.yaml) matches verbs ['play','listen to','open'] with ANY of ['recording of Charles and Rebecca','Charles and Rebecca recording','recording'], so the plain word 'recording' is enough.

CHANGES:
1. 1C prompt 4: replace it with a single natural imperative sentence that contains the word 'recording' (so it matches k_sl_1c_c_r2) and names no person; e.g. "Play the recording the logistics computer has stored." -- verify with the real storygame.runtime.candidate_matcher._matches_all that it matches exactly {k_sl_1c_c_r2} among k_sl_1c items, and that prompts 1-3 are unchanged. Update tests/test_1c_spine_prompts.py to the new prompt text expectations (keep the chain/eligibility assertions).
2. New tests/test_spine_prompt_names.py (hermetic): for each scene's array in frontend/e2e/canon-journey.js (parse the arrays with the same regex pattern used by the other test_*_spine_prompts.py files; all nine scenes), assert no prompt for that scene names a person/character that is not yet introduced in that scene. Find how the narration safety guard decides a name is 'unavailable' (grep storygame/runtime for 'unavailable entity' and read the surrounding code and narration_safety tests: it uses package knowledge/entity names and scene availability) and reuse that logic or its data (character names from data/stories/continuity-initiative/world.yaml, and which scenes introduce them) -- do not invent a new name list. If the guard's logic cannot be reused offline, implement the check as: collect protected/later-scene character names from world.yaml that the guard treats as unavailable for scene S and assert none appears (word-boundary, case-insensitive) in S's prompts. Run it; if it flags prompts in scenes you do not own (other than 1C), DO NOT edit them: list each finding (scene, prompt, name) in your notes and mark the test with pytest.mark.xfail(strict=False, reason=...) naming those scene ids ONLY for exactly those scenes, so the test passes today but reports them. 1C, 2A and 2B must pass cleanly.
